turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?
turns.patient_response: Hi, thank you. Um, well, I'm here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it really should. Just the idea of getting on a plane makes me... I just picture that really bad turbulence from my honeymoon flight all over again. I mean, I know people fly safely every single day, but I just can't seem to shake it.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an excessive and marked fear of flying that they recognize is out of proportion to actual risk, consistent with a specific phobia (situational type).

turns.doctor_question: Aside from when you're thinking about or planning a flight, do you ever have unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that turbulence experience popping up on their own?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. Um, it doesn't just pop up out of nowhere. I don't have nightmares about it or flashbacks or anything like that. 

It's really just... if I have to book a ticket or if I know a trip is coming up, that's when I start picturing it and get all worked up. But on a normal day at work or whatever, no, it doesn't cross my mind.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient explicitly denies having spontaneous intrusive memories, nightmares, or flashbacks related to the event.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from flying, do you notice similar intense fear or a strong urge to avoid other situations, like being in enclosed spaces or at heights?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. Um, I don't have any issues with heights or small spaces or anything like that. I take the elevator every day at work and it doesn't bother me at all. It really is just the flying.

turns.doctor_question: When you're actually at the airport or on the plane, do you experience an immediate rush of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I definitely do. It's actually not even just at the airport. Like, if I'm looking at flights for an upcoming conference, or honestly, even if I just hear a plane flying overhead, my chest tightens up right away. I get this sudden rush of panic, and I just feel like I need to shut my laptop or get away from the thought entirely. It's pretty immediate.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing an immediate rush of panic and chest tightening right away when exposed to plane-related cues.

turns.doctor_question: How long has this fear of flying been going on—was it right after your honeymoon flight, or did it start more recently?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it was right after. It's been going on ever since that turbulent flight back from my honeymoon. So, um, that would be about two years and five months ago now.
